name: FlowFieldGrid
src_typeComment: Scene wrapper around FlowField: defines the grid's world-space placement and auto-detects obstacles via physics overlap, so you don't have to hand-author a bool[,] yourself. Call RecomputeField() whenever the goal moves (once — not per agent); every FlowFieldAgent using this grid then shares that one result.

src_serialized.name: width
src_serialized.tooltip: Cells across / deep. Kept modest by default — cost is O(width*height) per recompute.

src_serialized.name: height
src_serialized.tooltip: Cells deep (Z axis). Kept modest by default — cost is O(width*height) per recompute.

src_serialized.name: obstacleMask
src_serialized.tooltip: Layers checked when detecting which cells are blocked.

src_serialized.name: obstacleCheckRadius
src_serialized.tooltip: Half-extents of the box used to test each cell for an obstacle — should be a little under half of cellSize to avoid false positives from a neighboring cell's obstacle.

src_serialized.name: obstacleCheckHeight
src_serialized.tooltip: World-space height the obstacle check box is centered at. Keep this above 0 (e.g. half an obstacle cube's height) — checking exactly at y=0 will false-positive against a ground plane's own collider, which sits flush with the grid's surface.

src_members.sig: public Vector2Int LastGoalCell { get; private set; }
src_members.name: LastGoalCell
BakeObstacles
src_members.comment: Scans the grid once for obstacles. Call again yourself if the level layout changes after startup.

src_members.name: RecomputeField
src_members.comment: Cheap to call often (e.g. every frame while chasing a moving goal) as long as the goal keeps landing in the SAME cell — the expensive O(width*height) pass is skipped unless it actually moved to a new cell. Still, for a genuinely fast-moving goal on a large grid, calling this every frame could be a real cost — consider throttling (e.g. every few frames) at larger grid sizes.
